thread:
alex: heads-up — after yesterday's client-proxy deploy I'm seeing client requests get routed to fallback buckets and quota attribution flips for some tenants. noticed during load test, not prod yet.
mina: ugh. which proxy? the internal routing-proxy or the new client-side shim?
tj: internal routing-proxy (v2) rolled at 02:30. logs? errors?
alex: v2 routing-proxy. no 5xx, just unexpected route headers. example from logs:
```
X-Route-Hint: tenant=acme;path=/generate;priority=low
X-Route-Map: shard=us-east-1;pool=dedicated-42
```
then console shows it as shard=us-west-2 and quota charged to tenant=default.
lucy: that header parsing code lives in the proxy metadata adapter. I pushed a small change last week re: `path` parsing (strip trailing slash). Could be a side effect.
mina: can you paste the raw TCP/HTTP dump for one of the failing requests? curious if the header got mangled in the proxy or client.
evan: here's a one-liner to capture header frames on the proxy host: `sudo ngrep -W byline 'X-Route' tcp and port 8080` — run it while repro.
alex: attached snippet from ngrep (sanitized):
```
GET /generate HTTP/1.1
Host: inference.redwood.ai
X-Route-Header: tenant=acme;shard=us-west-2;pool=dedicated-42
```
so the header arriving at proxy is already wrong (shard us-west-2). origin client sent us-east-1. looks like a rewrite inside our client-proxy handshake.
tj: aha — client-proxy does a best-effort normalization: it maps unknown shard aliases via the cluster mapping table. if the mapping table had an old alias `us-east-main -> us-west-2` that would explain. anyone updated mappings recently?
lucy: i touched the cluster mapping doc to add canonical names but didn't update the live mapping table; thought the sync job would pick it up. that sync job crashed on Tuesday and didn't retry.
mina: so two issues: (1) sync job failed, (2) normalization rewrites header to a canonical but wrong shard, causing quota attribution to fallback.
alex: is the sync job on the platform side? where does it run?
ev an: it's a cron in eng-platform namespace, `cluster-syncer` k8s job. logs show `panic: index out of range` at 03:12. I'm opening an incident.
mina: temporary mitigation: disable header normalization in the proxy (config flag `route_normalize=false`) and roll a canary. that should preserve original client header and keep attribution correct.
tj: +1. also add a safe-guard: if cluster-syncer hasn't updated mapping in >1h don't mutate headers (fail open).
lucy: i'll revert my doc change to avoid confusion and push a hotfix for the syncer to add better error handling.
alex: can someone create a small smoke-test that sends a few requests with different shard aliases and verifies console attribution? i can run it against staging.
mina: i'll sketch one in Python real quick and post gist.
mina: gist: https://gist.github.com/mina/shard-smoke-test (private) — it posts 10 requests and asserts tenant attribution matches header.
tj: deploy-bot: starting canary rollback for routing-proxy v2 -> v1 on 3 nodes in staging :hourglass_flowing_sand:
deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated by tj. Job id: job-8823. Rolling back 3/3.
alex: thanks. after rollback let's validate with mina's test, then roll the fix for syncer and re-enable normalization behind a feature flag (opt-in per-tenant).
lucy: noted. i'll also add a telemetry tag `route_normalized=true/false` so we can graph how many requests were normalized historically.
evan: opened incident: INC-2023-459, linked logs + stacktrace. tagging infra and platform.
mina: 👍 i'll ping QA to run the smoke-test after rollback.
alex: quick follow-up — do we need to update SDKs (python/go/ts) to stop emitting ambiguous alias names or is that separate?
tj: good call. let's add a lint rule in SDKs: block deprecated alias names at build-time and warn on runtime. canary that in go and python first.
alex: sounds good. thanks team. we should sync in 30 when job completes.
